literal.prompt: Какая императрица издала Жалованную грамоту дворянству в 1785 году?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The primary-library catalog identifies the original item as the Charter to Nobility, approved 21 April 1785, and says its opening text begins “we Catherine the Second” (turn1view0 L41-L43). The official library account states Catherine II signed the nobility Charter on 21 April (2 May) 1785 and distinguishes it from the same-day City Charter (turn2view0 L44-L46). The four options are Russian empresses; the named instrument and year select Catherine II uniquely. The retained Britannica URL had no body and is not used as evidence.

literalGroups.literal: Жалованную грамоту дворянству 21 апреля (2 мая) 1785 года подписала Екатерина II. Она закрепила привилегии дворян, включая освобождение от обязательной службы и податей.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The official library account dates Catherine II’s signature to 21 April (2 May) 1785 and says the Charter granted freedom from mandatory service and taxes (turn2view0 L44-L46). The proposed two sentences state those supported facts directly.

literalGroups.literal: Грамота закрепила за дворянами право владеть крепостными крестьянами.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The official library account lists the right to own serf peasants among the Charter’s nobility privileges (turn2view0 L46). This is a concrete added fact about Catherine II’s act.
The retained President Library collection period heading explicitly labels Elizabeth Petrovna’s reign as 1741–1761 (turn2view0 L208).

literalGroups.literal: В 1730 году Анна Иоанновна публично разорвала «Кондиции», отвергнув попытку ограничить её власть.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The official President Library article states that Anna Ioannovna publicly tore up the Conditions when she arrived in Moscow, resisting the attempt to limit her authority (turn3view0 L53-L54).

literalGroups.literal: После смерти Петра I его супруга Екатерина Алексеевна взошла на престол; это Екатерина I.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The official President Library article says that after Peter I’s death his wife Catherine Alekseevna succeeded to the throne (turn3view0 L44-L45), grounding the identification as Catherine I.
